questions.title: Location of the trigone
questions.question: The trigone is located in ……...

explanations.A: Incorrect. The apex of the bladder is its anterosuperior point, opposite the base where the trigone actually lies.
explanations.B: Correct. The trigone is a smooth triangular area on the inner aspect of the bladder base (its posteroinferior wall), in contrast to the folded (rugose) mucosa lining the rest of the bladder. Its corners are marked by the two ureteric orifices above and the internal urethral orifice below. This base location is the trigone's defining landmark.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ureter is a separate tube proximal to the bladder, not the site of the trigone itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The urethra begins at the trigone's lower corner (the internal urethral orifice) but is not itself the trigone.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The tip of the penis is part of the external genitalia, unrelated to the bladder's internal anatomy.

questions.learning_objective: State that the trigone lies on the inner aspect of the bladder base.

questions.title: Functional unit of the kidney
questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney is the ……..

explanations.A: Incorrect. The loop of Henle is one tubule segment within a nephron, not the whole functional unit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The renal pelvis is a collecting structure downstream of the nephrons, not itself the functional unit.
explanations.C: Correct. Each kidney contains roughly a million nephrons, the basic structural and functional units responsible for forming urine. A nephron comprises a renal corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman's capsule) plus a tubule system that reabsorbs and secretes before draining into a collecting duct. It is the whole nephron, not any single part of it, that performs the kidney's filtering function.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The proximal convoluted tubule is only one segment of a nephron, not the entire functional unit.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The distal convoluted tubule is likewise only one segment of a nephron.

questions.learning_objective: State that the nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter in right-margin column, p.53

questions.title: Structure surrounding the neck of the bladder
questions.question: The neck of the urinary bladder is surrounded by the ………

explanations.A: Incorrect. The external urethral sphincter is a skeletal-muscle sphincter surrounding the membranous urethra, not the bladder neck.
explanations.B: Incorrect. "Voluntary sphincter" describes the external, not internal, urethral sphincter, which does not surround the bladder neck.
explanations.C: Correct. The most proximal part of the male urethra, the intramural (preprostatic) part at the bladder neck, is surrounded by the internal urethral sphincter, a smooth-muscle sphincter under autonomic control that prevents retrograde ejaculation and involuntary leakage. This is distinct from the external urethral sphincter, a skeletal-muscle sphincter under voluntary control that surrounds the membranous part further downstream. The bladder neck and the intramural/preprostatic urethra describe the same anatomical region from two different reference points.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Skeletal muscle describes the external, not internal, urethral sphincter.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart, never in the urinary tract.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the internal urethral sphincter as surrounding the bladder neck (intramural/preprostatic urethra).

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter in right-margin column, p.53

questions.title: Longest part of the male urethra
questions.question: The longest part of male urethra is…….

explanations.A: Incorrect. The membranous part, passing through the urogenital diaphragm, is actually the narrowest and one of the shortest parts of the male urethra.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The prostatic part, passing through the prostate gland, is longer than the membranous part but shorter than the penile part.
explanations.C: Correct. The male urethra has four named parts — preprostatic (intramural), prostatic, membranous and spongy (penile) — and the penile (spongy) part, running the length of the penis, is the longest of the four. This is the same four-part classification under which the membranous part is separately known as the narrowest segment. The penile part's length reflects the distance it must travel along the shaft of the penis to the external urethral orifice.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Neck" refers to the bladder neck region, upstream of the urethra proper, not one of its four named parts.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The navicular fossa is a small dilated segment near the tip of the penile urethra, not the longest part overall.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the penile (spongy) part as the longest of the male urethra's four named parts.

questions.title: Formation of the renal pelvis
questions.question: The renal pelvis is formed by the union of……….

explanations.A: Correct. Urine collects from the collecting ducts into the minor calyces, which unite into the major calyces, which in turn unite to form the funnel-shaped renal pelvis. The renal pelvis is therefore formed directly by the union of the major calyces, the step immediately preceding it in this collecting chain. The renal pelvis is continuous inferiorly with the ureter.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The minor calyces unite to form the major calyces first; they do not unite directly to form the renal pelvis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Collecting tubules drain into the minor calyces, an earlier step in the chain, not directly into the renal pelvis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Renal pyramids are the tissue structures whose papillae project into the minor calyces, not the structures whose union forms the renal pelvis.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Nephrons are the functional units producing filtrate; several steps of the collecting system lie between them and the renal pelvis.

questions.learning_objective: State that the renal pelvis is formed by the union of the major calyces.

questions.title: Length of the ureter
questions.question: The length of the ureter is usually ………..

explanations.A: Incorrect. 25 inches is far longer than the ureter's true length, confusing the number with the wrong unit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 15 cm is shorter than the ureter's usual length.
explanations.C: Correct. Each ureter is a muscular tube continuous superiorly with the renal pelvis and continuous inferiorly with the bladder, measuring approximately 25 cm (closer to a 25-30 cm range in most descriptions) along its course. This is the standard teaching figure used for this exam. The other length options either shorten the true figure or swap the correct number into the wrong unit.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 10 cm is far shorter than the ureter's usual length.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 15 inches is far longer than the ureter's usual length, an incorrect unit conversion.

questions.learning_objective: State that the ureter is approximately 25 cm long.

questions.title: Part of the bladder receiving the ureteric openings
questions.question: The part of the urinary bladder which receives the opening of ureters is the ……

explanations.A: Incorrect. The neck of the bladder is where the urethra begins, the lower corner of the trigone, not the site receiving the ureteric openings.
explanations.B: Correct. The trigone's three corners are marked by the two ureteric orifices, where the ureters enter the bladder obliquely, and the single internal urethral orifice below. The trigone is therefore the part of the bladder that receives the ureteric openings. This oblique entry through the trigone also helps form a valve-like mechanism that resists the backflow of urine into the ureters.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The lateral surface is a separate part of the bladder wall, not where the ureters open.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The apex is the bladder's anterosuperior point, opposite the base where the ureteric openings actually lie.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The superior surface is a separate part of the bladder, not the site of the ureteric openings.

questions.learning_objective: State that the trigone is the part of the bladder receiving the ureteric openings.

questions.title: Length of the female urethra
questions.question: Length of female urethra is …...

explanations.A: Incorrect. 10 cm is longer than the female urethra's true length.
explanations.B: Correct. The female urethra is a short, roughly 4 cm muscular tube running from the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck, through the pelvic floor, to the external urethral orifice in the vestibule. Its short length, in clear contrast to the much longer male urethra, is clinically relevant as a factor in women's greater susceptibility to ascending urinary tract infection.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 20 cm is far longer than the female urethra's true length; this figure is closer to the male urethra's length.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 15 cm is longer than the female urethra's true length.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 25 (presumably cm) is far longer than the female urethra's true length.

questions.learning_objective: State that the female urethra is approximately 4 cm long.

questions.title: Termination of the female urethra
questions.question: Where is the termination of the female urethra?

options.A: At the vestibule behind the vagina
options.B: At the vestibule in front of the vagina
options.C: In the anterior wall of the vagina
options.D: In the neck of the urinary bladder
options.E: In the trigon of the urinary bladder

explanations.A: Incorrect. The female urethra's external opening lies anterior to (in front of), not behind, the vaginal opening.
explanations.B: Correct. The female urethra opens at the external urethral orifice in the vestibule of the vagina, the region between the labia minora, positioned anterior to (in front of) the vaginal opening. This anterior relationship to the vagina is the standard landmark for locating the external urethral meatus on examination. It follows the urethra's short course from the bladder neck through the pelvic floor to this external opening.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The urethra opens at the vestibule, external to the vagina, not within the vagina's own anterior wall.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The neck of the urinary bladder is where the urethra begins internally, not its external termination point.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The trigone is an internal bladder landmark at the urethra's origin, not the site of its external termination.

questions.learning_objective: State that the female urethra terminates at the vestibule, anterior to the vaginal opening.
